name: BlazeHive Connect
author: yassineblazehive

sections.description:
BlazeHive Connect links your WordPress site to BlazeHive, an SEO content service that researches keywords and writes conversion-focused SEO pages for your product or service. Once connected, finished pages are published to your site automatically — you never copy-paste HTML or fight your page builder.

Landing pages are published as a standalone, theme-independent layout: a keyword-specific hero, alternating image-and-text sections, a plain-English explainer, an FAQ, and repeated calls to action — the bottom-of-funnel structure that ranks and converts. The plugin renders each page from structured data stored in post meta, so the design is consistent on every WordPress theme and can be restyled later from a single stylesheet without touching your content.

What it does

  • Publishes automatically — BlazeHive pushes finished pages to your site through a secure REST endpoint. No manual export/import.
  • Full side-by-side layout — hero, alternating image splits, dividers, FAQ, and CTAs, rendered pixel-for-pixel the same on any theme (the plugin loads its own self-contained stylesheet and steps out of your theme’s way on landing pages only).
  • Its own URL space — landing pages live under /solutions/ (a post-type archive that lists them all, plus automatic inclusion in your WordPress sitemap). If your site already uses /solutions/, the plugin picks a free path automatically and tells you which one.
  • Clean SEO head — per-page <title>, meta description, Open Graph, and Twitter tags; canonical and robots handled by WordPress core.
  • Zero layout shift — every image ships with intrinsic width/height, so pages score well on Core Web Vitals.
  • Never breaks your site — if anything is malformed, the page renders a safe fallback (heading + description + call to action) rather than a blank screen. Your other post types are completely untouched.

Use your own post types

By default each content type publishes into its own BlazeHive post type, and that post type decides the URL root. If your site already has its own structure — a Resources post type at /resources/, Guides at /guides/, or plain pages — open BlazeHive → Advanced and point any content type at it. Those pages then live under your URL structure and are rendered by your theme like any other post of that type. Pages already published keep their post type and URL; only new ones follow the change.

Analytics

If you turn on Analytics in your BlazeHive account, the plugin sets it up on this site by itself. There is nothing to copy or paste.

  • It counts the people who visit your pages, with a small script from BlazeHive.
  • It shows which AI tools and search engines read your pages. These programs never run scripts, so the plugin tells BlazeHive about their visits from your server, after the page has been sent. Your visitors never wait for it.
  • Your own team is never counted when logged in.
  • If a cache plugin is active, the plugin asks it to let AI tools through, using that plugin’s own settings. Search engines keep getting the cached page, so your server load does not change. Turning Analytics off puts those settings back exactly as they were.
  • You can switch either part off at any time under BlazeHive in wp-admin. Your choice here always wins.

Nothing is sent and no script is added until Analytics is turned on in BlazeHive for this site.

Other BlazeHive page types

The plugin also registers post types for BlazeHive’s other formats — alternatives, “vs” pages, comparisons, and listicles — published as standard WordPress content.

Statistics pages

Statistics pages are pages of sourced, dated numbers on your industry, every number linked to the organisation that produced it, with a chart per section. Writers, journalists and AI answers cite them and link back. They live under /statistics/ with a styled hub at /statistics/ that lists every statistics page with its counts, and each page carries a contents list, a “Cite this page” box and links to your other statistics pages. The numbers on a page are fixed when BlazeHive makes it; nothing on the page changes by itself.

External services

This plugin is a connector for the BlazeHive service (https://www.blazehive.io) and needs a BlazeHive account to do anything. BlazeHive researches keywords, writes SEO pages and, if you turn it on, runs web analytics for your site.

1. Publishing

  • What is sent: when you connect, you paste the plugin’s API key and your site URL into BlazeHive. BlazeHive then calls this site’s REST endpoint to create and update posts. The content it sends (copy, image URLs, metadata) comes from BlazeHive and is written into your posts. Publishing sends no visitor data.
  • When: when you connect the site in BlazeHive and when BlazeHive publishes a page you approved.

2. Analytics (only when you turn it on in BlazeHive)

Analytics stays off until BlazeHive delivers an Analytics setup to this site, which only happens after you connect the site to your BlazeHive account and turn Analytics on there. You can switch each part off under BlazeHive in wp-admin at any time.

  • Visitor script: a script file is loaded from the BlazeHive analytics service (https://data.blazehive.io/js/script.js) on your public pages, for visitors who are not logged in as editors. In each visitor’s browser it sends to that service the page address, the referring page, the browser and device type, screen size, language and time zone. It stores random IDs in first-party cookies (bh_visitor_id, bh_session_id and two counters) so repeat visits count once. If you turn on “No cookies” in BlazeHive, it stores nothing in the browser. It does not store IP addresses.
  • AI and search bot visits: when a request to your site comes from a program whose user agent looks like a bot (AI assistants, AI crawlers, search engines), your server sends the BlazeHive analytics service the full page address, the user agent, the IP address of the request, the response status code and the time. This lets BlazeHive check that, for example, a visit claiming to be from an AI company really came from that company’s network. Requests from people are never sent.
  • Where it goes: only to the BlazeHive analytics service (data.blazehive.io), protected by a key for this site only. The plugin refuses any other address. If you run your own analytics service, a developer can allow its address with the blazehive_analytics_allowed_hosts filter.
  • Terms of Service: https://www.blazehive.io/terms-of-service/
  • Privacy Policy: https://www.blazehive.io/privacy-policy/

The plugin suggests text for your privacy policy under Settings, Privacy when Analytics is installed.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, choose blazehive-connect.zip, and click Install Now, then Activate (or install directly from the WordPress.org directory).
  2. Go to BlazeHive in your admin sidebar and copy your Site URL and API Key.
  3. In BlazeHive → Integrations → WordPress, paste both values and click Test connection.
  4. That’s it. Pages you approve in BlazeHive publish to your site automatically, at https://yoursite.com/solutions/<slug>/.
sections.faq:
Do I need a BlazeHive account?

Yes. The plugin is a connector — it publishes and renders content from BlazeHive. Without an account it registers the post types but has nothing to publish.

Will these pages look different from my theme?

Landing pages are intentionally rendered as a standalone, theme-independent layout so they look identical on every site and stay on-brand across your whole landing set. All your other content and post types use your theme normally.

What URL do landing pages use?

/solutions// by default, with a /solutions/ archive listing them all. If another plugin or page already owns /solutions/, BlazeHive Connect automatically uses the next free path (offerings, products, uses, or features) and shows you which one in the connection screen.

Does it slow down my site?

No. Pages render from data stored in your database. With Analytics on, people get one small deferred script. Bot visits are sent to BlazeHive after the page has been delivered, at most 20 times a minute, and the plugin pauses sending by itself if BlazeHive cannot be reached.

How do I turn Analytics off?

Under BlazeHive in wp-admin, untick “Count visitors” or “Send AI and search bot visits” and click Save. Your choice here always wins over the BlazeHive app. Deleting the plugin removes all of its Analytics settings.

What happens if something goes wrong with a page?

The plugin renders a safe fallback (heading, description, and call to action) instead of a blank page, and it never affects your theme or other posts.

How do I update the plugin?

Through WordPress as usual — Dashboard → Updates, or the Update link on the Plugins screen. BlazeHive will also nudge you from your dashboard when a new version is available.
sections.changelog:
2.8.0

  • New: Analytics, with nothing to set up. Turn on Analytics in BlazeHive and the plugin installs it here by itself: visitor counting, and a report of which AI tools and search engines read your pages.
  • Bot visits are sent from your server after the page is delivered, so visitors never wait. Sending is capped per minute and pauses by itself when BlazeHive cannot be reached.
  • Works with cache plugins: WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, WP Super Cache, W3 Total Cache and WP-Optimize are asked, through their own settings, to let AI tools through. Search engines keep the cached page. Turning Analytics off restores their settings exactly.
  • A new Analytics card on the BlazeHive screen shows what runs and has two switches. Your switches always win.
  • Safe by design: the script and the bot reports only ever use the BlazeHive analytics service. No other address is accepted, even with your BlazeHive key.
  • Suggested privacy policy text under Settings, Privacy.
  • Deleting the plugin now removes its Analytics settings.

2.7.0

  • New: statistics pages. Pages of sourced, dated numbers on your industry, with a chart per section, a contents list and a “Cite this page” box. They live under /statistics/, with a styled hub at /statistics/ that lists every statistics page.
  • Landing pages have a new, more modern layout: a centred hero, framed images, numbered sections, an FAQ you can open and close, and a closing call-to-action panel. They use your brand colour and support a dark mode for dark sites. Existing landing pages switch to the new layout the next time they are published.

2.6.2

  • Article headings now keep a little space above them, so a page whose heading follows an image no longer looks glued to it.

2.6.1

  • Removed a leftover style rule that tried to hide your theme’s post title on BlazeHive pages. It did nothing on the pages BlazeHive renders itself, and on themed pages it risked hiding the only heading on the page. Your theme’s heading is now always left alone.

2.6.0

  • New: publish into your own post types. Under BlazeHive → Advanced, point any content type at a post type you already use, so pages land under your existing URL structure and your theme renders them. Applies to pages published from then on; anything already live keeps its post type and URL. “Reset config” puts every content type back to its BlazeHive default without touching a single published page.
  • BlazeHive never overwrites your content: when a page it publishes would collide with a post of yours that has the same slug, WordPress gives the new page a unique slug instead. Your post is left exactly as it was.
  • Every BlazeHive URL root now steps aside if your site already uses it. Alternatives, comparisons, and listicles got the automatic fallback that landing and FAQ pages already had, so the plugin can no longer collide with an existing page or another plugin’s post type.
  • Sites that already publish under the default roots keep them — your live URLs never change on update.
  • “{Your product} vs Competitor” pages now publish as comparisons, under /comparisons/, instead of their own /vs/ root. One less URL root to manage, and both page styles live in one archive. Any existing page of that kind is moved automatically and its old address redirects.
  • Fixed: images inside article pages could overflow their container on themes that do not constrain images. Every image now ships with a maximum width, so it fits whatever layout renders it.
  • The FAQ hub at /faq/ lists every question, including ones published into one of your own post types.

2.5.0

  • BlazeHive pages now render your site’s own header and footer. Previously landing, FAQ, and article pages were standalone documents with no navigation — a visitor arriving from Google had no way back into the rest of your site, and the pages were poorly linked internally.
  • Works with both classic themes and block (full site editing) themes.
  • Fixed: pages could ship two
  • Your theme’s stylesheet now loads on these pages so the header and footer look like they do everywhere else. BlazeHive’s own styles remain scoped to its content and cannot restyle your theme.

2.4.0

  • New contextual-linking endpoints: your connected BlazeHive account can now list your published posts and place a hyperlink on a phrase that already exists in your content (used by BlazeHive’s contextual link features, which you opt into from your BlazeHive dashboard).
  • Linking never writes or rewords anything — one link is wrapped around one existing phrase, in body paragraphs and list items only, at most one link per target site per post. Block markup and special characters are preserved exactly.
  • All new endpoints require your site’s own API key, like every other plugin endpoint. No publishing behavior changed.

2.3.0

  • Article pages (alternatives, vs, comparison, listicle) now render with the same clean, theme-independent styling as landing and FAQ pages: consistent typography, spacing, tables, images, and code blocks on every theme.
  • Article pages get a proper H1 (the post title) and social preview (Open Graph/Twitter) tags, using the first body image when available.

2.2.0

  • Post type keys renamed from the generic bh_ prefix to the distinctive blaz_ prefix (blaz_landing, blaz_faq, …), per WordPress.org plugin review.
  • Existing content is migrated automatically on upgrade — every page keeps its URL, status, and content.
  • The publish API still accepts the old post type names, so no BlazeHive-side change is needed.

2.1.0

  • New: FAQ pages. BlazeHive can now publish one-question-one-answer pages, each rendered as a clean, theme-independent page with a breadcrumb back to the FAQ hub.
  • New: automatic /faq/ archive — a styled hub listing every published question as a card grid, ordered alphabetically (falls back to /faqs/ if your site already uses /faq/).
  • FAQ pages get the same per-page SEO head (title, meta description) as other BlazeHive content.
  • New: social preview (Open Graph/Twitter) tags on FAQ pages and the FAQ archive.
  • Fix: on block themes, landing pages (and the new FAQ pages) no longer output a duplicate

2.0.6

  • All admin and front-end CSS/JS now loads through the WordPress enqueue system (no inline style/script tags).
  • JSON-LD output hardened: script-safe encoding so stored markup can never break out of the tag.
  • Rendered-page cache now sets an explicit expiration.
  • Removed an unnecessary core file include; admin menu moved to a standard position.
  • Internal functions and constants renamed to the full blazehive prefix.
  • Refined landing page spacing and image framing.

2.0.5

  • Landing pages render as a full, theme-independent side-by-side layout (hero, image splits, results, FAQ, CTA) from structured post meta.
  • Automatic /solutions/ archive as an internal-link hub, with slug-collision fallback if the path is already taken.
  • Per-page SEO head (title, meta description, Open Graph, Twitter) and zero-CLS images.
  • Safe fallback rendering so a malformed page never white-screens.
  • Fix: block data containing quotation marks is now stored and rendered correctly.
  • Distributed and updated through WordPress.org.

upgrade_notice.2.8.0: Adds BlazeHive Analytics. It stays off until you turn it on in BlazeHive. Publishing works exactly as before.
upgrade_notice.2.5.0: BlazeHive pages now carry your site's header and footer, on both classic and block themes, and no longer emit a duplicate title tag alongside Yoast or Rank Math.
upgrade_notice.2.3.0: Alternatives, vs, comparison, and listicle pages now look polished on every theme, matching the landing and FAQ page treatment.
upgrade_notice.2.2.0: Internal rename of post type keys (bh_ to blaz_) for WordPress.org compliance. Existing pages migrate automatically; URLs are unchanged.
upgrade_notice.2.1.0: Adds FAQ pages: a styled /faq/ hub plus theme-independent question pages published straight from BlazeHive.
upgrade_notice.2.0.6: Hardening and polish: enqueued assets, script-safe JSON-LD output, cache expiration, and refined landing page spacing. Recommended for all BlazeHive users.
